subject: humanities
passage: In the eighteenth century, opera audiences sat in auditoriums that stayed lit by candles throughout the performance, and many people bought printed copies of the libretto, the text of the opera, to read along as the singers performed. In 1876, however, the composer Richard Wagner had the auditorium darkened during performances at his new theater in Bayreuth, Germany, and over the following decades many opera houses adopted the practice. In darkened theaters, audience members who did not understand the singers' language most likely ______
stem: Which choice most logically completes the text?

choices.A: relied more heavily than before on reading printed libretti during the performance.
choices.B: stopped attending operas that were sung in languages other than their own.
choices.C: found it harder to follow the words while the opera was being performed.
choices.D: asked theaters to keep their auditoriums lit during Wagner's operas.

explanation.why: Audiences had used printed libretti to follow along, which required light. Once auditoriums were darkened, they could no longer easily read during the performance, so those who did not know the language would have more trouble following the words.
explanation.A: Incorrect. Reading a printed libretto requires light, so a darkened auditorium would make this harder, not more common.
explanation.B: Incorrect. This goes too far: the text shows that following the words became harder, not that people stopped attending.
explanation.C: Correct. Without light to read the libretto, listeners who did not know the language would lose their main way of following the words.
explanation.D: Incorrect. The text says nothing about audiences making requests to theaters.
